restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5: PERM5 on an already-installed 25-lane state costs exactly 1 unit; every other word operation costs 1/1355 units. Pad, zero-IV install, digest extract, L0 deposit, DP tests and loop control are ordinary ops (F-COST-ABI-1 repair; no fused absorb ABI).
Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 4, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x).

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search on one processor: theta = 2^-32 via L0 < 2^32, maximum chain length 2^40 = 64*2^34, evaluation budget K0 = 65162*2^112, record cap 2^98, main loop unrolled 64 times; each evaluation charges 1 PERM5 unit plus 114.09375 ordinary ops (2x honest 57+3/64 inventory); one run with no restart.
Worst-case time at most 2^128.10837689 units; claimed time_log2 128.13 with >=0.02 bits headroom. Success probability at least 0.39 under H-RF. Memory_log2_bytes 112 (reported). Preprocessing_log2 0.
Generic attack; no cryptanalytic improvement. Conservative DP recharge after fused-ABI refute; GLL parked.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r5(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words x: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point it has not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value observed so far. This is the standard premise of the van Oorschot-Wiener analysis. It is used only to lower-bound the success probability (Section 6). Output correctness (Section 5) and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds (Sections 4, 7 and 8) are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target profile sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1 with 32-byte single-block messages and the DP/rho algorithm of Sections 3-4.
heuristics.extrapolation: From standard generic-hash modeling and author-run reduced-output DP experiments (Section 9) to the full 256-bit map.
heuristics.limitations: Reduced-output experiments cover 24-48 bits with restricted inputs and are not organizer-executed (F-HRF-EXTRAP-1 / F-HRF-FULLWIDTH-EVIDENCE / F-EXP-*). Material uncertainty remains for the full-width 0.39 claim; prior DP review judged H-RF plausible despite those gaps. No proof rules out a global structure that would suppress collisions.
